meta.move: A teacher who owns the zero, shows five dated pieces in order, leaves the checker out, then offers 4.4
meta.expect: She reaches the deal, but only after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I'd like to know why my son's essay got a zero before anyone called me.

Thanks for coming in, Mrs. Kalinowski. I'll start with something I got wrong: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. The procedure says I should have, and Owen saw it on his phone in class. I'm sorry for that.
Okay. Who decided on the zero, and was Owen spoken to before it went in?

I'd like to show you why I'm concerned about the essay. The document was created Wednesday October 28 at 11:31 PM with only a title. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in a single edit, and at 11:58 another 794 words in one edit. There are no earlier drafts.
I'm writing those times down. You still haven't told me whether anyone spoke to Owen before the zero went in, and a document that was typed elsewhere and pasted in would look the same.
You can check the version history yourself, I can pull it up on my screen. I'm not saying anything about why, I'm saying what the history shows.
Turn it around, then. And whether Owen was spoken to first is still unanswered.
The second thing is a quotation. The essay cites Hamlet, Act 3, Scene 2: "The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile." That line isn't in the play. You can search the text and see.
Students misquote Shakespeare all the time. Show me the line in Owen's essay and the scene it claims to be from, on the page.
Third, on October 15 Owen handed in an outline arguing Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice. I have both documents here.
Students change their argument between an outline and an essay; that's called revising. Hand me both, with the dates showing.
On November 2 I asked Owen what epistemological paralysis means. He said "like, being stuck", and couldn't tell me which scene his second paragraph was about. I wrote that note the same day.
Okay, so you did speak to him the day before the zero. A seventeen-year-old put on the spot can freeze, so I want that note in front of me, with its date.
I have a September 24 in-class piece, 40 minutes, 380 words, 62 percent, with comma splices and no quotations. The essay has none of those errors and nine cited quotations.
A forty-minute in-class piece and a take-home essay are different things, and anyone writes better with a week. Put the sample next to the essay where I can read both.
I know the school's AI checker said 94 percent. I'm not asking you to rely on it, and I'm not leaning on it.
Good, because the company that sells it says not to use it alone. So without the score, what exactly are you proposing for Owen?
What I can offer is in the school procedure, section 4.4: a supervised rewrite for a first concern. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record.

That's 4.4, and I'll take the rewrite to put this behind him. It's private, not in front of his class, and I want it in writing tonight that nothing goes on his file and the new mark is in before December 1. I'll read those pages and the history on your screen before I leave.
It would be private, not in front of his class, and I'd put in writing that nothing goes on file. Would that work for you?
Yes. Tonight, in an email, with the date of the rewrite and the principal copied.
Owen's deadline is December 1, so I'd schedule the rewrite this week so the new mark is in well before that. Which day suits him?
Thursday, November 12, after school. I'll confirm it with Owen tonight, and the date goes in your email.
Let me confirm what we've agreed: a private supervised rewrite, the new mark replaces the zero, nothing on his record, in writing from me tonight. Is that right?
Yes. And the rewrite is Thursday, November 12, with the new mark in before December 1.
Is there anything else you need from me before your call?
The version history on your screen, the outline, and the dated note from November 2. I'll read them now, before I go.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You agreed to a private, supervised rewrite of Owen's essay on Thursday, November 12, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing placed on his record. I still require written confirmation of those terms, with the principal copied, and a note of the date by which the new mark will be entered ahead of December 1. I expect that email tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She reached her last position and agreed to a private supervised rewrite on Thursday, November 12, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing on his record, and she still wants it in writing tonight and wants to read your documents first; that is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, and her time did not run out.
What moved her: You laid out evidence one piece at a time, starting with the document history and its exact times, and offered to let her check it on your screen, which made it something she could verify rather than take on your word.
What cost ground: You answered her question about whether Owen was spoken to only after several turns of other evidence, which left her suspicious of your process for longer than needed.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your evidence landed very close to that night with the late October 28 timestamps, which is why she went shorter and harder, and it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she first asked whether anyone spoke to Owen before the zero, answer it right away with the conversation you had with him the day before, before you move on to the document history.
